column1: # Key of the Carl Pawel cipher (lead 2179, BSB Clm 10382 n. 46, 1624), rebuilt by Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5 agents), 5 Nov 2026.
# Licence: CC BY 4.0, Brice Dudout. German letter cipher; each letter has three homophones in a block of three consecutive numbers.
# It is the alphabet of targets/casimir1629 (Johann Casimir to Camerarius, 1624-29) moved down by 3: number here = casimir1629 number - 3.
# Frozen before the held-out test: casimir1629 KEY (as frozen for that target, SHA-256 d8b9e735...) shifted by 3, the shift chosen on scan 181
# (0.921 of the glossed letters there, next best 0.737); held-out scan 182: 13/13 letters (validation.txt).
# As in casimir1629, 41-43 = p and 68-70 = y are taken from the published casimir1629 key (corrected there after its own test); the frozen
# key had 41-43 = p (from "pars" on scan 181) and 68-70 = i. Neither block occurs in the held-out part.
# Numbers 83 and up would be the nulls of casimir1629 (86 and up) moved by 3: not seen here. 1-10 and 53-55 not seen.
# number<TAB>letter<TAB>seen in training: glossed runs of scan 181 with status ok (count)<TAB>note
